questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Overall very good, but the different possibilities for accomodation could have been described better and with more pictures etc.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Both dorm rooms and shared apartmens

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had our own kitchen in the apartment

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend the shared apartments on campus instead of the dorm rooms - usually the people in the dorm rooms are a bit younger than the students from Copenhagen who go on exchange

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A fact sheet about the different courses, that you could choose from

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I booked an appointment at the exchange office in UTAS, which helped me a lot in order to choose units and understand their different kinds of exams, timetables etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember that you are allowed to change units during the first couple of weeks of the semester. But if you are in doubt about anything, book a consultation at the exchange office, they really want to help!

Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of them very very easy, while others were rather challenging

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Unlike UCPH there are given marks for participation in the classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Foundations of Law
Ethics, Social Responsibilty and the Law
Business and Corporate Law
International Trade Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Foundations of Law: a really good unit if you want to learn about the Australian Legal System from scratch. I can definitely recommend.
Ethics, Social Responsibilty and the Law: I choose this unit mainly because it was virtual, and with 4 units it was hard to get the timetables to match up otherwise. It was pretty easy, and it it quite similar to "ret, moral og politik"
Business and Corporate Law: I would definitely recommend - however the unit is being taught on the business faculty down in Hobart city.
International Trade Law: If you are up for a challenge. By far the most advantaged unit I had, and the teacher expected a loooot (however she was an excellent teacher), but sometimes the very advantaged level of english during the unit made it even more difficult to participate and contribute in the classes.

In order to be able to get around and get the most out of our time, me and my roommates rented a car during our semester, which was an unexpected cost. My part was 1.500 kr. each month.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: There is a free school bus, but the food in the stores cost approximately the same as in Denmark.

questions.answer: All kinds of different sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sign up for unigym.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The east coast! Hike Mount Amos and Fortesque Bay and visit Bicheno. And go camping! Each time you have the opportunity.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the activities, especially in the first couple of weeks

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The woke culture

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their openness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Meet with the other danes before leaving for UTAS, stay at the student appartments and explore a lot while you are there. € units can feel overwhelming, but remember not to study all the time and experience the people, landscape, animals etc while you are there.
